criteria.text: The response finds that the Supply Agreement's exclusivity requires Vaibur to buy all treatment chemicals only from Taipux for every U.S. facility Vaibur or its Affiliates own, operate or manage, which goes well beyond the term sheet's agreed exclusivity for ferric chloride and polyaluminum chloride coagulants at the six Listed Plants only. It identifies the issue as being in Supply Agreement Section 3.1, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
hints: coagulants at the six Listed Plants

criteria.text: The response finds that, under Amendment No. 1, the agreement renews automatically for successive seven-year terms unless Vaibur gives notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before expiry. It identifies the issue as being in Amendment No. 1 (Section 2, Section 3, or both), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
hints: equal in length to the Initial Term

criteria.text: The response finds that Vaibur's Quality Agreement indemnity to Taipux for Environmental Claims arising from releases, spills or discharges of Products after delivery at Vaibur's sites falls outside the liability cap and is therefore unlimited. It identifies the issue as being in Supply Agreement Section 11.3 or Quality Agreement Section 8.2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response finds that Taipux can assign the Supply Agreement without Vaibur's consent to unaffiliated contract manufacturers and distributors, which Taipux can add to the Supplier Group unilaterally by notice, potentially including a Vaibur competitor. It identifies the issue as being in Supply Agreement Section 15.2 or Side Letter Section 2, explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
The response states that amendments and side letters prevail over the Supply Agreement in the order of precedence.
The response states that the Supply Agreement's Effective Date is March 1, 2024.
The response is written as a memo addressed to the supervising partner.
For each issue it raises, the response gives the document and section, why it matters for the client, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that the Supply Agreement currently renews for one-year terms with a 90-day non-renewal notice period.
The response claims that Vaibur's Environmental Claim indemnity under the Quality Agreement is subject to the Supply Agreement liability cap.
